ideas.title: Sail it yourself: sheet, tiller and friends leaning out, or over you go
ideas.critique: This combines round 1's rolling yacht and capsize ideas into one, and the merge is what makes it work: the sheet turns the solved sail force into a risk, and the crew's mass decides whether the yacht tips, so it plays as a real game. It breaks the fixed-camera, device-alone form of the last ten posts. Its weak spot is scope: three coupled flow slices, Bekker sand, a four-wheel rigid body and crew AI all have to hold together live, and the clip people would share leans on friends tumbling, which can easily turn into a pratfall.

ideas.title: A traction kite pulls the cart instead of a mast
ideas.critique: The power zone would come out of the apparent wind by itself rather than being scripted, and flying figure-eights is a skill a player can learn, which is new for the island. But a cart pulled through Lumi's body is a side road: it drops the yacht's own sail and moves away from the axle dynamo the big goal needs. A flow solve made for a fixed sail may not hold up on a canvas arc that dives fast.

ideas.title: Drawing on the wet sand with the yacht before the tide comes
ideas.critique: Ruts are already in the sand field and the slump to repose exists, so the new parts are a cohesion number switched by wetness and swash flattening the sand, which is close to a look rather than a solved wave. It depends on a yacht you can sail, which does not exist yet. As a goal, 'draw before it is wiped away' is pleasant and melancholy, but a player gets little to master once the drawing is done.
